gaps.sentence: We were asked to ___ an experiment in the laboratory.
gaps.explanation: do an experiment is the standard collocation in scientific contexts.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: Why don't we ___ lunch together on Friday?
gaps.explanation: have lunch is the standard collocation for eating lunch.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune by buying his train ticket in advance.
gaps.explanation: save a fortune means to avoid spending a large amount; buying in advance keeps money.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
The children ___ great fun at the party.
gaps.explanation: have fun / have great fun is the fixed collocation; 'made fun' means mocked someone.
